出版者的话

古希腊圣哲亚里士多德曾说：‘任何人都会生气，这没什么难的，但
若要适时适所地以适当方式对适当对象恰如其分地生气，可就难上加难
了。’我们现在讲的情绪管理指的就是要适时适所地对适当对象恰如其分
地表达情绪。

现实生活中，人们越来越多地认识到情绪管理能力的重要性，因为
这方面能力出众的人往往在各个领域都游刃有余；相反，此项能力差的
人，虽然可能很聪明，但做起事来往往很吃力。

情绪管理能力虽部分得益于先天因素，但归根结底还得靠后天的学
习和培养。幼儿时期是情绪管理能力培养的黄金时期，一个人在幼儿时
期所获得的情绪经验和习惯会在大脑中形成永久的神经联结，对其身心
发展影响很长远。

当前，亲子共读情绪管理类图画书这种情绪管理能力培养方式已被
广泛认可。优质的图画书好比幸福的种子，通过父母的声音飞进孩子的
耳朵里，植根在孩子的心底，施以阳光、雨露就能生根、发芽。

这套有趣的动物图画故事书温情脉脉，每一本都是有针对性地就孩
子的某一种情绪话题展开，描绘孩子的心路历程，揭示其走出情绪困扰
并解决问题的过程。每一本书都附有幼教专家精心撰写的导读，可作为
家长亲子共读时的参考。

让我们在这套书的陪伴下，去享受一段美妙的亲子阅读之旅吧！

Publisher's Note

The ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle once said: 'Everyone gets angry, and that's not difficult. But to get angry at the right time, in the right place, in the right way, and with the right person, to the right degree—that's difficult indeed.' What we now call emotional management is precisely about expressing emotions appropriately, at the right time and place, toward the right person, and to the right extent.

In real life, people are increasingly recognizing the importance of emotional management skills, because those who excel in this area often thrive in various fields; conversely, those who lack this ability, although possibly very intelligent, often find things difficult.

Emotional management skills may partly stem from innate factors, but ultimately, they must be cultivated through learning and practice. Early childhood is the golden period for developing emotional management skills. The emotional experiences and habits acquired during this period form permanent neural connections in the brain, profoundly influencing a child's physical and mental development.

Currently, the method of parent-child co-reading emotional management picture books is widely recognized as an effective way to cultivate emotional management skills. High-quality picture books are like seeds of happiness, carried into children's ears by parents' voices, taking root in their hearts, and with sunlight and rain, they can grow and flourish.

This series of engaging animal picture storybooks is warm and heartfelt. Each book focuses on a specific emotional topic for children, depicting their inner journey, revealing how they overcome emotional difficulties and solve problems. Each book includes a carefully written guide by early childhood education experts, serving as a reference for parents during parent-child reading.

Let us enjoy a wonderful parent-child reading journey with this series!

Teacher Says to You
A Kitten Belonging to Childhood
I finished reading this story with a smile. This naughty little kitten reminded me of my own childhood. Back then, when I was naughty and unhappy, I would hide in the small forest near the village, alone, watching flowers, grass, and trees, tasting various wild fruits: wild grapes, sour plums...
I think children might be the people in this world who understand small animals the most. They have an almost innate, unbreakable closeness and affection for small animals like kittens and puppies. The younger the child, the more they seem to be able to happily and harmoniously interact with animals. Of course, this trait can be traced back to the perspective of biological evolution, since humans are originally part of nature! But I prefer to understand it from the perspective of child psychology.
This little kitten is lively, energetic, naughty, playful, and imaginative. Almost everything he sees, he can quickly think of ways to play with it. These traits are so similar to the energetic children around us. He seems to be a representative of adorable and innocent children! At the same time, the kitten's qualities of not giving up easily when facing problems, loving to think, and always finding ways to solve problems, have made me even more firmly believe that as adults, we should trust the inner strength of children and protect their innate confidence, curiosity, and desire to explore.
